summary: End-to-end verified the new Airbnb-style 'When / Add dates' search segment + react-day-picker range calendar popover on both Home (/) and Stays (/stays). All 9 acceptance criteria pass on desktop (1280x900), tablet (768x1024) and mobile (390x844). The popover is portal-rendered to <body>, has a non-zero bbox, is never clipped by the search pill's overflow-hidden, and the calendar is fully visible on every viewport. Live date-range filtering on /stays works: applying Jun 30 – Jul 7 reduced listings from 14 to 13 and switched the page from grouped layout (6 'Stays in ...' headings) to a flat grid (0 headings) with the URL updated to ?checkin=2026-06-30&checkout=2026-07-07.

verification_details.home_clear_link: After selecting range and clicking hero-when-clear, trigger reverted to 'Add dates' — PASS

critical_code_review_comments: WhenPicker.jsx line 141 reads window.matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)') only at mount of the popover render. If a user opens the popover, resizes the window across the 768px breakpoint, and re-interacts, the calendar may keep the old numberOfMonths until next open. Acceptable for now (popover usually closes on resize-like interactions) but consider wiring matchMedia + addEventListener('change') to a state to make it reactive.

Past-date disabling uses `disabled={ before: new Date() }` (line 142). new Date() is captured each render but only when the popover is open — fine. However, a user who keeps the popover open across midnight could see yesterday still selectable for ~1ms after midnight; not a practical concern.

Stays.jsx hides the When trigger on mobile (<sm) inside the pill. Acceptable per the requirement, but mobile users currently have NO way to set dates from the visible search pill — they must open Filters. Consider adding a small calendar icon in the mobile pill that opens the Filters modal directly to the dates section, to improve discoverability.

The popover uses z-[60] backdrop and z-[61] popover. The site's WhatsApp floating widget (bottom-right) sits at a similar z range; verified visually it is behind the backdrop, so OK. Worth a code comment noting the z-index contract.
context_for_next_testing_agent: WhenPicker (react-day-picker v8.10.1, portal-rendered) is working end-to-end on Home & Stays. Notes for future testing: (1) live env's 'today' is around Jun 28 2026 (NOT Feb 2026 as the request hint claimed), so future dates begin Jun 28+. Pick Jun 30 – Jul 7 in tests (those are visible in the default month view). (2) DayPicker day buttons have no aria-label; select them via 'button.rdp-day:not([disabled]):has-text("N")'. (3) Range start/end cells get classes .rdp-day_range_start / .rdp-day_range_end and middle cells .rdp-day_range_middle for visual assertions. (4) Stays cards have data-testid pattern 'stays-card-{uuid}'. (5) Applying a date range on /stays switches the page from grouped 'Stays in {area}' headings to a flat single grid — assert by counting group headings dropping to 0. (6) Regression from iteration_27 (search-bar / nav overlap) still holds — no new overlap introduced.
rca_of_the_issue: n/a — no bugs found. Feature was implemented correctly: createPortal(..., document.body) properly escapes the search pill's overflow-hidden clipping; portal popover is anchored to viewport center via fixed inset positioning; backdrop and Escape both close; Clear empties state; Apply propagates ISO YYYY-MM-DD strings back to parent which feeds URL params and live filter.
